lessons.title: Separate discovery, identity replay and proof scope
lessons.when: Any finite search, modular experiment or certificate promotion.
lessons.use: Freeze inputs and bounds; verify exact identities; state the mathematical implication and its hypotheses. Record independent replay, formal proof and external review separately.
lessons.avoid: Interpreting a completed box, matching hash, numerical residual or good-prime success as a theorem outside its scope.
lessons.boundary: Source hashes establish integrity. They do not establish mathematical correctness or independent implementation.
lessons.reopen_when: A new exact certificate closes the missing implication.

lessons.title: Saturate the intended geometric open before elimination
lessons.when: Collision ideals, Fitting modules, boundary components or resolved Riemann–Roch modules.
lessons.use: Identify the boundary and wrong-thickness factors, saturate by the required open, and retain a certificate of the resulting ideal or module.
lessons.avoid: Counting degenerate collision factors or imposing independent rows on conditions with resolution-graph syzygies.
lessons.boundary: Saturation changes the geometric locus. Every excluded factor and its interpretation must be explicit.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed problem uses a different open or a genuinely new boundary stratum.

lessons.title: Audit the exact universe, not just totals
lessons.when: Finite support, orbit, chart or parameter censuses.
lessons.use: Reconstruct the ordered universe; require one record per key; compare explicit predecessor unions with the final complement. Keep a cheap coverage audit separate from elimination replay.
lessons.avoid: Using aggregate counts or the complement of the last batch to certify that all earlier cases were actually closed.
lessons.boundary: A complete finite census remains limited to its basis, degree, roster and equivalence relation.
lessons.reopen_when: The universe, equivalence relation or mathematical coverage argument changes.

lessons.title: Use the binary closure and finite cutoff
lessons.when: Starting another binary GVC promotion or low-degree search.
lessons.use: Start from the Hall-envelope closure and finite-certificate note; use its proved rational decision procedure and operator-independent cutoff.
lessons.avoid: Reopening the prime-dependent Hall/carry promotion route as if unrestricted binary GVC were still open.
lessons.boundary: The Hall/carry subtheorems remain useful; their parked promotion statement is neither proved nor needed by the closure. Ternary minimum degree and efficient polarization are separate questions.
lessons.reopen_when: A task explicitly concerns the historical promotion statement or a hypothesis outside the binary theorem.

lessons.title: Distinguish pure-moment vanishing from SIC failure
lessons.when: A semistable point has a long or all-order zero pure-moment sequence.
lessons.use: Test a fixed multiplier and its mixed tail, using an all-order identity when claiming failure. Preserve the Rodrigues point as a negative control for moment–nullcone equality.
lessons.avoid: Treating semistability plus pure-zero moments as a mixed-moment counterexample.
lessons.boundary: The bidegree-(3,3) Rodrigues orbit is SIC-safe despite falsifying moment–nullcone equality. Dense bidegree-(3,3) classification remains open.
lessons.reopen_when: A new multiplier has an exact infinite nonzero tail, or a new all-order safety theorem applies.

lessons.title: Prove recurrence boundaries before inferring all-order vanishing
lessons.when: Compiling sparse contraction moments into hypergeometric sums.
lessons.use: Choose independent lattice coordinates, retain factorial zero conventions or explicit boundary terms, and certify the recurrence including its singular indices.
lessons.avoid: Inferring an all-order zero identity from holonomicity or a bounded zero prefix alone.
lessons.boundary: The holonomic-framework note supplies methods, not a new universal moment cutoff.
lessons.reopen_when: A recurrence, its boundary contributions, initial conditions and required ordinary-point hypotheses are certified.

lessons.title: Close a normalized full ideal before extending support-by-support searches

lessons.use: Retain the residual linear-x coefficients, perform the justified linear eliminations, and use the exact rational unit-ideal certificate for the full quadratic space.

lessons.reopen_when: The ansatz has higher degree or a hypothesis outside the certified ambient-quadratic space.

lessons.title: Use the corrected motion frame and keep the master equivalence scoped

lessons.when: Varying the elliptic equation while preserving its cubic two-division field.

lessons.title: Reuse adaptive principal-dependency construction and keep fixed-word obstructions scoped
lessons.when: A factor-base relation matrix or bounded BNF attempt is proposed for rank arithmetic. Also applies when attempting to continue a successful specialized principal dependency with a family parameter still variable.
lessons.use: Distinguish maximal-order/local computations, selected factor-base image, class-group generation and certified full2-rank. Measure noncanonical relation coverage before widening a comparison. Before writing another collector, read the successful adaptive small-ideal principal-relation constructor on MW16-05 at3/17: it constructed two additional strict classes without exceptional points. Extra-class construction and a full class-group upper bound are distinct tasks. For the published rank-28 control, reuse the proved discriminant factors and exact theta=-3*x+1 reduced-field map; both original and reduced fields already reach the same BNF relation plateau. Preserve all1676/1572 principal atoms and their generic corrections. Define the varying cubic algebra, every element formula and the specialization homomorphism before discussing parameter dependence; specialized prime-ideal columns have no default common coordinate system. Test valuation cancellation in the full continued word before substantial computation. A reusable constructor may choose a fresh dependency at each parameter. For a fixed output, bind a finite collision-prime set through exact denominator, leading-coefficient, normalization and nonzero-resultant data before interpreting isolated valuation obstructions. A square norm alone does not preserve the arithmetic dependency. Freeze the constructor policy across parameters and rebuild all arithmetic objects. For a small transfer panel, freeze rank-blind inputs and equation aliases before arithmetic, cap lifting at the first two independently new classes, and separately meter preparation, dependency construction, compaction, failed attempts and verification. If historical cost is incomplete, record a subtotal and meter commissioning instead of substituting post-construction lifting time. Stage transfer spending: require cold reference class-to-point certification before two fixed paired fresh fibres, then require one fresh success before the remaining six. Snapshot all transitive code packages for detached work; retain and charge startup failures rather than resetting the commissioning meter. Test source-snapshot imports as well as source-tree arithmetic.
lessons.avoid: Calling deficiencies1905/1890 from the sparse two-field pilots full class-rank estimates, or escalating a generic BNF timeout without a new arithmetic plan. Do not reverse-engineer only closing atoms, interpolate specialized coefficients and call it a mechanism, or interpret a presentation-dependent vanishing minor as class creation. Do not require an adaptive constructor to reuse one atom word or one low-genus parameter family, or confuse the resultant-defined collision-prime set with the control bad primes or a finite diagnostic prime window. Do not port the reference by copying atoms or ideal-coordinate arrays, keeping a strict-dimension-six assertion, or assuming every dyadic residue degree is one. Do not replace difficult frozen fibres. Separate rank totals do not establish complementarity; certify the combined subgroup after both arms seal. Reusing only the successful tail collector with an empty relation pool does not reproduce the complete historical constructor. Declare the cold warm-up and test actual dependency creation; a formally large quotient or many independent atom rows is not success.
lessons.boundary: The two pilots and their bounded skew-sieve extension found zero/one noncanonical relations with no new independent relation in the extension. Deficiencies1905/1890 remain factor-base-image bounds; a generation argument is required for a full class-group bound. Missing data remain UNKNOWN. The separate MW16-05 positive constructor remains valid; both frozen covers now have independently verified blind lifts. The sparse two-field pilot does not invalidate it. Its factor-base-1000 pilot has 172 canonical principal rows, zero noncanonical relations and displayed deficiency 141 below the generation bound 1202640; none is an S-class or Selmer bound. The complete coefficientwise continuation of column6 is now defined and obstructed: an exact full-product coprimality certificate gives odd valuations at twelve good geometric parameters. Any parameter cover making this specific word a point class has genus at least5. This does not obstruct the soluble class at3/17, alternative formulas or arithmetic incidence conditions; it is not a reason to launch a higher-genus search. The fixed column6 word now has only finitely many rational Selmer specializations: its local parity condition confines it to finitely many signed genus5 twists, and Faltings proves finiteness. The exact finite prime set is bound by105 integer guards and1693 nonzero integer-resultant circuits, with independent replay. Its primes and twists are not enumerated, and no effective parameter list follows. This closes that output template without restricting a constructor selecting different dependencies. The eight-input transfer preflight verifies selection and128 point equations. The authorized metered commissioning adapter is now frozen and launched; reference generic16 independence and cold field preparation pass. Relation collection has begun, but the full reference cost and fresh transfer remain UNKNOWN. A launch and toy arithmetic tests are not class-to-point success. Before handover the frozen cold class bank completed in321.67 elapsed seconds, collecting841 atoms from23244696 tested norm pairs. Replay of retained projected parity records has rank841 and kernel dimension0; strict extraction and lifting were not reached. This binary replay does not independently recertify all atom factorizations. The class commissioning gate therefore fails; only the already authorized independent V3 reference arm finishes, after which the controller stops without fresh fibres. No automatic bank enlargement follows, and this cold-start bank miss does not invalidate the earlier successful constructor with its longer relation warm-up.
lessons.reopen_when: For full class-group bounds, sufficient independent relation coverage and generation certificates are still required. For prospective class/point construction, a separately scoped parameter-dependent constructor may choose new dependencies with full provenance and independent local and rational-lift certificates. The fixed column6 template is closed by a finiteness theorem; neither higher-genus twist searches nor fixed-output retries are suggested.

lessons.when: Transporting sections through a binary-quartic Jacobian or covariant map.

lessons.title: Optimize the measured dominant phase
lessons.when: Proposing a runtime improvement or comparing two research runners.

lessons.use: Recognize the candidate height form, choose a low-degree polarization and solve the line-incidence kernel. Verify both incidences and nonincidences, compile the residual cubic pencil with a rational origin, then measure section rank before proving heights, saturation and the Picard upper bound.

The degree-four O+P+Q polarization supplies fifteen lines; the first seventeen displayed sections have rank fifteen, and two further conics complete rank seventeen. This is inverse construction conditioned on known exceptional points, not a prospective parameter selector.
