lessons.when: Exact image membership for the two-slice derivation D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y.
lessons.use: Group expressions by target weight, compute one standard basis of the primitive module per group, then lift each query and verify D(primitive)=expression. Reuse those primitives across ideals. Build the quotient image of ker(D) by closure under u, v and w; require the frontier to become empty.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding the same module for each seed or treating a finite iteration cap or arbitrary y-degree truncation as kernel-image closure.
lessons.boundary: A membership answer is exact only after the primitive and kernel correction tests succeed. Pure/mixed exponent windows remain bounded experiments. The 128-step guard fails if closure does not stabilize; it is not a completeness bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The derivation, coefficient ring, ideal or target-weight module changes; otherwise reuse the existing compiler and declared inputs.

lessons.title: Apply the principal and plinth-power theorems before searching
lessons.when: Choosing an ideal for the rank-two model LND or reusing its old conductor search queue.
lessons.use: First test whether the ideal contains a power of (u,v), or is nonzero principal. The plinth-power theorem LND-NPF and complete principal theorem LND-CPM give all-order safety. The five historical nonprincipal charts all contain (u,v)^3.
lessons.avoid: Expanding old NPL/PDP/PCD power windows or treating the rational-root ladder as the current end of the principal classification.
lessons.boundary: These theorems concern the stated rank-two derivation and ideal classes. Genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside plinth-power saturation, and different derivations, retain their own obligations.
lessons.reopen_when: An explicitly specified ideal lies outside both completed classes, with an all-order theorem or counterexample target.

lessons.title: Use the lowest valuation face in conductor arguments
lessons.when: Clearing Laurent denominators in the invariant-affine principal LND families.
lessons.use: Pass to the associated graded ring for the relevant prime valuation. The lowest negative face carries the required power of the carrier. Apply pure vanishing at growing moment orders to force positive valuation, which eventually clears every fixed multiplier denominator.
lessons.avoid: Claiming carrier divisibility for every negative Laurent coefficient: u^2*y^3 contains the coefficient w^3/u in the rational-root chart, which is not divisible by q1-w.
lessons.boundary: Theorems 6.8–6.16 use lowest faces and explicitly controlled denominator losses in the model LND. The stronger coefficientwise statement is false and cannot be used as a shortcut.
lessons.reopen_when: A new carrier has a proved associated-graded divisibility statement and a compatible denominator bound.

lessons.title: Keep pointwise equations after cohomological compression
lessons.when: Reducing the cubic or higher Danielewski contraction equations.
lessons.use: Compile the small de Rham flux ledger and leading pencil first, then retain the lowest nonzero coefficients of J-1 for each degree and boundary-pole profile. Use the explicit normalized cubic family in CL25 as a regression against any claim that flux plus leading face is sufficient.
lessons.avoid: Launching the unstructured 90-variable cubic ideal, replacing J=1 by its cohomology class, using opposite signs for P'(i) and P'(-i), or quotienting by automorphisms that do not preserve the chosen degree filtration.
lessons.boundary: The 11 nonconstant flux equations are necessary. The exhibited family satisfies them all but fails J=1; both boundary derivatives equal -2. A degree-bounded quotient needs filtration-preserving transformations.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete chart classification adds the missing pointwise conditions or proves a degree-preserving normal form.

lessons.title: Reuse the finite Rees atlas and finish the surface ledger
lessons.when: Continuing the quartic weighted graph normalization or Hilbert-polynomial calculation.
lessons.use: Start from the three completed side point bases, eight-cone corner atlas and exact side-to-corner packet matches. The next finite calculation records divisor classes, Rees multiplicities, polarization restrictions and normal-bundle degrees of the center curves; apply centerwise Riemann–Roch and the existing endpoint conductor corrections before one global pushout.
lessons.avoid: Repeating ambient normalI runs that produced no certificate, redoing the completed local principalizations, or equating matching conductor colengths with equality of quotient sheaves.
lessons.boundary: The modular graph multidegree and two unknown coefficients alpha/beta remain a calibration. Local normalization and a finite-model Euler-characteristic formula do not prove global normalization, flatness or equinormalization.
lessons.reopen_when: The actual missing surface-intersection or gluing data are supplied, or a changed model invalidates the existing atlas.

lessons.title: Restrict later local rows to the existing kernel
lessons.when: A large RR ambient has a smooth block with a small exact modular kernel.
lessons.use: Match ambient labels and hashes, then restrict actual sparse component rows to the small kernel. Check every rational denominator at the chosen prime and bind the independent smooth-block rank/kernel certificate. Full stacked column rank mod p then certifies the same bounded rank over QQ.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding a dense stacked matrix, computing node layers after the kernel is already zero, or using a smooth-kernel record from a different pole bound.
lessons.boundary: A surviving modular direction is not a rational pencil. A full-rank minor rejects only the supplied ambient; it gives no exhaustive pole bound. The good-reduction consumer trusts the independently recorded smooth rank/kernel and does not reconstruct that matrix.
lessons.reopen_when: A different, mathematically justified ambient has a compatible smooth-kernel certificate.

lessons.title: Keep product divisibility distinct from a rectangular jet
lessons.when: A resolved normal-crossing chart reduces a global pole condition to Z^a*Y^b divisibility.
lessons.use: Identify the actual principal ideal before forming a quotient. Impose compatible componentwise divisibility and overlap gluing before extracting any finite residual corner. In the recorded node t^17=Z^51*Y^68 times a unit.
lessons.avoid: Replacing the one-dimensional quotient R/(Z^51*Y^68) with the finite length-3468 quotient R/(Z^51,Y^68), or expanding a raw ten-generator ninth-power ideal before clearing chart units.
lessons.boundary: A rectangle and a product impose different conditions. Pareto-leading rows are necessary conditions; equal-leading terms and unit expansions can still interact.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact component/gluing argument identifies a finite residual quotient without changing the ideal.

lessons.title: Bind replay schemas to the exact marked section
lessons.when: An old module or physical-target script is reused after a section-normalization correction.
lessons.use: Use the primitive height-24, degree-ten q8 section and the full R*h*Dy=Ny*Dx normalization. The corrected marking wrapper dispatches the 2cover implementation. The corrected QQ checker reconstructs the section from q6 points and consumes the frozen tracked component-nef target.
lessons.avoid: Renaming the new marking JSON to the old filename, accepting its new status in old consumers, or applying the historical degree-192 branch result to a different chord input.
lessons.boundary: The old consumers require the withdrawn NS-decomposition schema; the finite-module script asserts collision degree 46. Missing q6 Jacobian/zero/E7-section inputs are a recovery gap, not permission to rebuild a campaign or evidence that q8 remains unsolved.
lessons.reopen_when: The original inputs are recovered with matching hashes, or a separately verified schema/marking transport is supplied.

lessons.title: Use factor supports to avoid all pair products
lessons.when: A complete finite set of rational quadratic covers is tested for q_i*q_j=q_k.
lessons.use: Canonicalize rational sign/prime atoms and odd monic polynomial factors. A two-branch-point cover has at most two finite polynomial atoms: only an edge with its singleton endpoints or a triangle can give a three-character relation. Test candidate support XORs with the full constant squareclass. The alternate11952 frame has 39,147 distinct irreducible quadratic atoms, so it has no candidate support relation.
lessons.avoid: Forming hundreds of millions of polynomial pair products, discarding rational constants by making a branch polynomial monic, or treating a formal variable rename as transport between two bases.
lessons.boundary: Complete orbit and equation attachment must be established separately. A found relation still needs a base/height certificate. The old rank-28 and q_103b2 curves have base degrees 8 and 9 over alternate11952, so they are not quadratic characters there.
lessons.reopen_when: A new source has actual repeated/two-factor supports or certified new degree-two characters on the same base.

lessons.title: Stream the short shell and retain the quotient
lessons.when: The short-vector list is too large although the finite quotient and one representative per orbit are small.
lessons.use: Use a unimodular LLL basis with an explicit row-coordinate transport, stream Fincke-Pohst leaves, and retain parity masks, multiplicities and canonical representatives. Evaluate every accepted norm exactly and require equality with an independent exact PARI count before asserting completeness. Export representatives in the pinned frame.
lessons.avoid: Materializing nearly three million signed vectors just to recover 39,147 M/2M classes, or confusing LLL column transforms with row-vector coordinates.
lessons.boundary: Floating pruning and a generous guard are not themselves a completeness proof; exact leaf membership, uniqueness of coordinate visits and the matching exact count are essential. Lattice coverage still does not construct branch equations.
lessons.reopen_when: The lattice, norm bound or equivalence relation actually changes; the existing complete frame tables should be reused otherwise.

lessons.title: Use the disjoint graph only for equation cost
lessons.when: Selecting two bisections for a rank-19 biquadratic construction.
lessons.use: Use XOR with norm-four masks to identify all disjoint representatives when that lowers equation cost. Test Galois-character independence by the exact quadratic squareclasses and then use the appropriate lifted height theorem.
lessons.avoid: Using membership in the 8,895,801-pair disjoint graph as a hard filter for independent characters, or restarting its common-cover scan after complete bisection injectivity.
lessons.boundary: All common-cover pairs in the published smooth-bisection frame are excluded. Distinct-character biquadratic rank 19 is a separate construction; both the published pair and the recorded low-complexity pair lie outside the disjoint graph.
lessons.reopen_when: A different geometric objective specifically requires disjoint representatives, or genuinely new quadratic characters are supplied.

lessons.title: Close a failed incidence bank before enlarging a speculative carrier hypothesis
lessons.when: Trying to propagate a frozen exceptional Kummer block into an infinite rank-gain subfamily.
lessons.use: Keep the full integral frame, physical zero and I2 component; enumerate signed norm10/14 vectors with exact LDL arithmetic and an explicitly incomplete prefix at a node stop. Compile actual curves by the marked trace RR identity, including the A1 vanishing condition. Require nonzero rational splitting at the control before exact cubic-field labels, then normalize the fixed-line fibre product and certify its rational infinitude. Finite-reduction neighbourhoods can make the eventual output condition effective. First count extensions over the fixed t-line with constant squareclasses retained. Translation identifies normalized covers, so a completed nonsplitting miss excludes its entire generic-translation orbit. Pairing cannot supply a missing constituent lift. Close a stopped bank before returning to the successful arithmetic dependency.
lessons.avoid: Replacing the rank17 frame by its rank16 MW height matrix, calling a lattice vector a curve, identifying constant twists or arbitrary independent base changes, treating one genus-one point as infinitude, or choosing generic corrections independently at different places. Do not infer low-intersection rational bisections from soluble extra strict classes, count formulas as independent arithmetic directions, or treat a failure before label matching as evidence against the marked block.
lessons.boundary: The stopped MW16-05 prefix supplies182 exact genus-zero bisections with182 distinct extensions, all nonsplit at3/17. The control values represent182 distinct rational squareclasses, without an independence claim. There is no common obstruction among the real place and primes at most1009;21 fail by sign. Both shells remain incomplete,73 split residuals and candidate171 remain separate. Translation and pairing cannot rescue these completed incidence misses. No marked rank18 family or strict/ideal transfer is constructed; the conditional propagation theorem remains valid.
lessons.reopen_when: Only a new theoretical connection from the actual arithmetic dependency to a different carrier hypothesis would justify a separately scoped proposal. This bank is closed; no shell completion, enlargement or interrupted-candidate repair is scheduled.

lessons.title: Cancel the Jacobian of the actual source chart
lessons.when: A primitive-polynomial derivative is used to design a mask suspension.
lessons.use: Compute the chart Jacobian first. In the A4 root algebra, interpolate H^3/(4K^3L) in the four conjugate roots and factor its denominator B^2*rho*sigma. Carry the selected field generator and exact residual divisor through every change of chart.
lessons.avoid: Substituting 1/P'(T) for the required chart reciprocal: the derivative split preserves the four-sheet field but leaves H^6/(2*Theta*K^6*L^3) in the ordinary chart. Do not confuse coefficient gcd in a nonnormal presentation with divisorial cancellation on its normalization.
lessons.boundary: The localized fourfold determinant-one map still has genuine poles. Its existence does not supply a polynomial affine source; the original masks and Hhat continuation are already closed.
lessons.reopen_when: A different chart or coupled source/target construction has a new exact divisor ledger and a field-recovery argument.

lessons.title: Normalize and reject the boundary before reconstructing coordinates
lessons.when: A coarse deletion passes unit, class-group and ampleness screens.
lessons.use: Count actual simple/triple primes on the normalized incidence, then use its seven-curve lattice. Test forced-column content before enumerating completions. The strict B column has content two, excluding every boundary basis containing it. For a surviving split, test indispensable horizontal genera before presenting a coordinate ring.
lessons.avoid: Using the four-curve coefficient-plane matrix upstairs, trying to fix a nonprimitive forced column by adding primes, or rebuilding the B-free coordinate ring after Hhat and q14 were shown to have genera 13 and 20.
lessons.boundary: The B-free split passes local lattice/ampleness tests but is not A2. The lattice rejection is stable under polynomial extension; the separate surface-boundary genus proof is not automatically a universal stable-cancellation theorem.
lessons.reopen_when: A genuinely different selector has rational horizontal boundary components and survives the normalized divisor exact sequence.

lessons.title: Check the conductor before trying a multiple of a boundary prime
lessons.when: A rational component is non-Cartier but has finite local index at one singularity.
lessons.use: Purify the height-one ideal first: (q2,S103) has an embedded finite contamination, while (q2,L) is the intended conic prime. Examine every non-Cartier point. At the other quadratic pair the conic is divisorial on one normalization branch and only codimension two on the other; conductor matching forces an extra height-one zero for every positive multiplicity.
lessons.avoid: Treating the A3 local index two as a reason to try doubling, or treating one rational norm factor as a selector whose entire horizontal boundary is rational.
lessons.boundary: KIG25 excludes all positive principal divisors supported only on this conic. It does not exclude other rational-horizontal selectors or a genuinely coupled ideal-contraction construction.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed prime or normalization/conductor incidence is different, with an exact gluing argument.

lessons.title: Compile branch jets and a norm floor before factoring selectors
lessons.when: Searching polynomial masks with prescribed normalized exceptional orders.
lessons.use: Reduce forbidden coefficients of all seven truncated branch jets modulo c^2+27 and solve exact rational linear algebra. Reuse V2,1=0, V2,2=<T^2>, the six-dimensional V3,1 and its root-quadratic extension. The pole-degree leading form gives the sharp norm floor 16 and rules out root-quadratic directions below degree 24.
lessons.avoid: Brute-force coefficient searches below a proved degree floor, or scoring the near-selector J as almost viable because only one branch jet fails. Its first exact correction is linked to Hhat by syzygies and has an absolute genus-31 strict curve.
lessons.boundary: The floor covers total degree at most three and root degree at most two. The higher correction module and other root charts remain open; satisfying all valuation jets does not imply rational boundary.
lessons.reopen_when: A specified higher-degree jet space or different valuation row changes the exact kernel problem.

lessons.title: Remove fixed components and use the value-gradient kernel map
lessons.when: A selector norm has high degree but a known birational root chart.
lessons.use: Remove fixed K^3 before analyzing the curve: the degree-16 norm plane becomes a strict net of degrees 9,10,10. Replace the three moving-singularity equations by the value-gradient determinant -54*M^2*D23 and its generic kernel map of degrees 19,18,18. Audit exceptional rank drops of M separately.
lessons.avoid: Repeatedly normalizing large expanded norms at random heights, counting a fixed-component rank drop as a new exact selector, or claiming the 864/144 height samples classify the parameter plane.
lessons.boundary: D23 is known, but its full parameter image is not implicitized. The first rational conic member retains positive genus and its isolated principal route is closed. Generic integrality and bounded boxes do not settle every degeneration.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact parameter-image calculation, chart cover or new critical-locus intersection produces a different admissible candidate.

lessons.title: Search the smaller selector space and retain reduction exceptions
lessons.when: Looking for nonlinear factors of a small linear system over a finite field.
lessons.use: Factor all 3906 points of P5(F5) in the six-dimensional A4 selector space rather than enumerating every projective cubic coefficient vector. Reuse the classified factor list and tangent kernels. For conics, all 3875 degree-two forms have been screened; the exceptional monic-U^2/s0 lift tree dies modulo 625.
lessons.avoid: Launching the same finite-field or 175680/58095 rational census again, or promoting a lift obstruction in one chart to a characteristic-zero classification. Do not discard degree loss, reducible reduction or the artificial H-factor neighborhood.
lessons.boundary: Only U=0 is a rational affine line in the full root-linear space, by exact resultant gcds. Nonlinear rational factors remain possible in the specified structural/degree-drop neighborhoods. The eight H-slice lift levels are bounded evidence.
lessons.reopen_when: A precise formal neighborhood or reduction exception outside the closed charts has a new theorem-directed test.

lessons.title: Use independent affine-source rejection gates
lessons.when: An affine modification passes smoothness, factoriality or flexibility tests.
lessons.use: Keep units, class group, ML, Derksen, Hodge/topology and explicit coordinate recognition separate. SL2 passes the early algebraic tests but has class L^3-L and S^3 topology. The smooth rho=h model has class L^3 yet class group Z/2. Exact invariant failures can reject a candidate before a large mixed-incidence solve.
lessons.avoid: Calling matching invariants an affine-space isomorphism, treating a rational/logarithmic determinant-one lift as an ordinary polynomial Keller map, or requiring two modified p,q,r outputs when the retained-block argument only proves at least one.
lessons.boundary: The remaining S4 mixed-incidence problem is finite only after degree and support are fixed. It still needs constant full Jacobian, degree-six field preservation, mask reconstruction and an actual affine-space recognition proof.
lessons.reopen_when: An asymmetric coupled construction supplies the missing divisibilities and explicit source identification.

lessons.title: Reject CAS interpreter errors even after a success marker
lessons.when: A Singular subprocess is used to certify identities, factor lists or a finite census.
lessons.use: Use singular_runner.py for the audited A4, F2 optional bridge and tagged-lift callers: reject interpreter diagnostics and nonempty stderr, require a unique terminal marker, and check expected result markers as complete lines. The many-channel RESULT adapter keeps historical program hashes and timeout records, but discards stdout on interpreter failure so downstream parsers cannot retain an apparent unit or rank.
lessons.avoid: Trusting returncode==0, subprocess check=True, a later PASS substring, or absence of a reported factor. An intentional ERROR followed by PASS exits zero on the locally inspected Singular 4.3.2.
lessons.boundary: The base guard has six small protocol tests and earlier tiny real interpreter controls. The RESULT adapter has four additional tests plus mocked many-channel/tagged integration; no GVC moment, elimination or census was replayed. The 19 many-channel substitutions preserve the AST of all mathematics, generated programs and timeouts. Historical outputs are not fresh guarded executions, and other CAS wrappers remain outside this audit.
lessons.reopen_when: A new interpreter version or output protocol changes diagnostic/completion behavior; cover that behavior with a tiny test before authorizing any research replay.

lessons.title: Calibrate local signatures against known quotient directions
lessons.when: A local Kummer signature rank is proposed as an exceptional-rank or Selmer predictor.
lessons.use: Use the rank-28 control: the generic seventeen and all twenty-eight points both have signature rank 15 in 53 coordinates, despite eleven globally independent quotient directions. At odd p compare known-image rank with v2(c_p*#E_ns(F_p)); equality certifies full local coverage. Keep the p=2 formal group separate.
lessons.avoid: Reading zero incremental local rank as zero global quotient gain, treating a smooth local point as everywhere-local solubility, or treating capped and timed-out lifts as obstructions.
lessons.boundary: Four odd places and infinity are covered; seven odd places and p=2 remain unresolved. The pilot has 60 witnesses and 24 inconclusive tests. Exact public point covers supply residual lower bound 11, but no ambient Selmer upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete ambient squareclass construction and all local conditions are available, or a different signature is tested against these positive controls.

lessons.title: Record whether visibility predicts or fits a known point
lessons.when: Comparing a multisection atlas against known high-rank fibres.
lessons.use: Freeze the atlas and cost order before targets; record genus, degree, family dimension and incidence codimension. The rigid rational-bisection span ranks are 5,3,2,1, but individually named degree-two generators number 4,0,0,0. All 38 displayed generators admit a genus-one degree-two member fitted after seeing the point, using the common norm-eight trace -P2-P5.
lessons.avoid: Calling a post-hoc moving-pencil interpolation predictive, equating span rank with the number of exposed named generators, or constructing millions of rational trisection equations just to fit already known points.
lessons.boundary: Only degree-two rational curves and the 320 deep norm-26 trisection classes are complete. The norm-20 and degree-four equation sets are samples, and degrees five/six were stopped, not excluded. The quotient is the displayed L_t/M_t, not a saturated full Mordell-Weil group.
lessons.reopen_when: A predeclared pencil gives a genuinely new target, or a target-directed rational multisection solves one of the remaining named-generator obligations.

lessons.title: Eliminate first and retain every good-reduction hypothesis
lessons.when: Seeking a two-node genus-two bisection with rational quadratic normalization.
lessons.use: Use the finite-pole chord M=M0+(l0+l1*u)h^2. In q=(u^2+a*u+b)^2*(c2*u^2+c1*u+c0), eliminate the three c coefficients from the top terms before solving the four essential variables. Intersect full quadratic squareclasses, including scalar characters, at distinct primes. Reconstruct coordinatewise only with compatible trace bases, then factor over QQ and check both section identities.
lessons.avoid: Dropping the scalar squareclass, trusting incompatible chart labels, promoting an empty affine multi-prime intersection to a global theorem, or treating standard CRT reconstruction as an unlimited rational-height search.
lessons.boundary: The recorded primes 17,23,29,31,37 and modulus 13005833 give no accepted candidates in the reconstructed boxes. Infinity, simultaneous bad reduction and larger heights remain open. The separate complete singular genus-one row gives first possible arithmetic genus at least two, not equality.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact infinity/bad-reduction chart or an unbounded covering theorem supplies information outside the completed boxes.

lessons.title: Reuse exact local lift failures and retain singular branches
lessons.when: Searching for a second anti-invariant section of a direct singleton twist.
lessons.use: For chi=3 and P.O=0, use the exact polynomial box deg X<=6, deg Y<=9. Fix the smooth infinity point, solve lower Y coefficients recursively, then classify tangent rank. Full-rank extra branches admit digit-by-digit exact lift tests. Reuse the 2423 recorded nonlifting certificates and the known-section depth-512 reconstruction control before another shell.
lessons.avoid: Re-enumerating the 10,690,517,260 recorded X candidates, interpreting nonlifting of isolated extras as closure of singular/known-section reductions, or allowing producer-source drift to trigger a campaign rebuild.
lessons.boundary: The result covers 400 distinct shells for 200 ranked characters only. The other 38947 characters, P.O>0 and nonsingleton covers remain open. The retained-record auditor checks source/data integrity and coverage without rerunning arithmetic; its per-run digest cache invalidates on file changes.
lessons.reopen_when: A new mathematical argument addresses singular reductions, another degree box or a separately justified character set.

lessons.title: Check the exact source image before tangent calculations
lessons.when: A coordinate change produces a finite Laurent support envelope.
lessons.use: Build the binomial-jet image matrix and retain its linear relations. The F2 r=3 images have ranks 74/83 and 196/215; the formal terminal point violates a primitive source relation by 3470256. Reject such a base point before interpreting its tangent dimension.
lessons.avoid: Treating every supported monomial as an independent source coefficient, or treating a tangent at an invalid base point as a component.
lessons.boundary: The r=3 literal polynomial projection is already excluded by its length-27 top-gap algebra and unit Q gap. Full Laurent cross terms remain unaccounted for; finite r=4/5 samples do not establish an all-r theorem.
lessons.reopen_when: A proved tail correction or a different exact source image changes the projection problem.

lessons.title: Separate carrier strata before number-field specialization
lessons.when: Specializing a coefficient system at classified carrier parameters.
lessons.use: Branch first: the rational squarefree cofactor is outside the movable-double-root component. Compute double-carrier operators over Q(rho), rho^2-3rho+1=0, using exact quotient-field arithmetic; the defect ratio adds the independent quadratic 27y^2-9y+1 and gives four embeddings of one quartic compositum.
lessons.avoid: Plugging the squarefree cofactor into a double-root chart, or replacing exact number-field kernels by floating-point ranks.
lessons.boundary: The 82 squarefree spacings are routed but not eliminated. Specialized linear maps do not decide the nonlinear ideal.
lessons.reopen_when: A new carrier stratum or a theorem covering its full target-and-tail component is supplied.

lessons.title: Keep divisibility conditions when factoring an operator
lessons.when: Factoring a common Laurent divisor before projecting nonlinear forcing.
lessons.use: First retain the Euclidean remainder against the forced factor, then project the quotient in its exact cokernel basis. In F2 the coupled obstruction is 294 divisibility jets plus 53 quotient coordinates; the final block is seven target and six Hermite coordinates after earlier endpoint controls.
lessons.avoid: Keeping only the 53 normalized quotient equations, or mistaking thirteen final cokernel coordinates for thirteen source variables.
lessons.boundary: These are presentation dimensions. The complete circuit has 954 reachable variables and its component remains undecided.
lessons.reopen_when: A new proved elimination removes the discarded-factor constraints on the precise localized component.

lessons.title: Carry endpoint solutions as a shared arithmetic circuit
lessons.when: Large nonlinear forcing is assembled after exact triangular eliminations.
lessons.use: Intern field constants and repeated arithmetic nodes, carry the 1489-term endpoint substitutions, and propagate the 134 upper Q eliminations before projecting all remaining rows. Evaluate the DAG and sparse Jacobian without expanding a multivariate polynomial list. Higher formal coefficients use the fixed Jacobian and its left cokernel.
lessons.avoid: Expanding the whole source presentation before specialization, or rerunning the forcing regression merely to inspect its counts.
lessons.boundary: The compact JSON stores digests and summaries, not the 710439-node DAG. Full replay rebuilds it; the retained-checkpoint audit is only an integrity and metadata check.
lessons.reopen_when: The exact circuit or mathematical component changes, or a separately scoped replay is needed.

lessons.title: Check the target value separately from formal continuation
lessons.when: A modular Newton direction or finite formal homotopy appears unobstructed.
lessons.use: Use exact line-polynomial gcds for line exclusions and project each formal forcing into the full left cokernel before solving the next coefficient. Preserve the gauge, field, order, denominators and target residual. The regular F31 order-16 jet still fails 50 equations at lambda=1; F61 supplies an order-8 checkpoint, not a characteristic-zero lift.
lessons.avoid: Calling same-field Newton a Hensel lift, inferring a multivariate obstruction identity from finitely many tangent lines, or evaluating a truncated jet at lambda=1 as if convergence were proved.
lessons.boundary: The gcd-one result excludes its specific whole line. The 112 coordinate and eight dense lines do not reconstruct the entire obstruction map; finite jet recurrence patterns do not prove rationality.
lessons.reopen_when: A reconstructed branch passes the complete circuit at the target, or an exact ideal certificate closes the component; characteristic-zero and global realization remain separate.

lessons.title: Back-substitute by pivot column, not discovery order
lessons.when: Sparse Gaussian elimination discovers pivots out of column order.
lessons.use: Back-substitute in descending numerical pivot-column order and check J*delta against the requested right-hand side. Retain a regression whose pivot discovery order is y,x: reverse insertion order gives the wrong solution. F2 also keeps the full 153-dimensional left cokernel when testing obstructions.
lessons.avoid: Reversing a pivot dictionary or using only the inconsistent-row indices as an obstruction basis.
lessons.boundary: This repairs the linear solve; a consistent tangent equation still need not integrate to a solution.
lessons.reopen_when: The solver, pivot policy, prescribed-coordinate gauge or field representation changes.

lessons.title: Verify the geometric bridge before enlarging a permutation census
lessons.when: Local Kummer data are proposed as branch cycles of a global cover.
lessons.use: Read the actual carrier map first: PF2CW1 makes the simple squarefree points unramified, invalidating both historical transposition applications. Retain the conditional censuses as regressions. Their S11 certificate generates all 330 three-cycles from intersecting A6 supports; repeated star connectors give an all-degree coarse witness.
lessons.avoid: Re-enumerating 11! permutations or more degree bounds to settle a bridge already contradicted by the carrier theorem; confusing residue-cover product one with a global Keller meridian completion.
lessons.boundary: The conditional S7/S11 covers neither realize nor exclude F2. A terminal A6 residue quotient and a global transitive group are different data.
lessons.reopen_when: A different actual carrier has a proved ramification and attachment theorem matching the proposed permutation model.

lessons.title: Transport original valuations and transverse poles together
lessons.when: A translated Laurent chart is used to compile a source boundary graph.
lessons.use: Undo the translation before assigning original orders: the terminal normal gives nu(x),nu(y_old),nu(x*y_old^5-c)=(-25,5,12), not a monomial ray (-25,17). At each interior residue-node preimage also inspect the transverse coefficient: its order -2 requires two source blowups.
lessons.avoid: Using residue incidence alone to count attachments, or charging the root matching length 54 as a logarithmic point correction.
lessons.boundary: The later exact cyclic root contribution is 27 and the outgoing tail contributes zero. These local results leave the affine purity divisors and effective global Chern filtration unresolved.
lessons.reopen_when: A new coordinate change or actual global boundary packet changes the full valuation and logarithmic-unit data.

lessons.title: Use the existing ternary counterexample before designing another lift
lessons.when: A proposed GVC experiment starts by purifying the rank-five SIC witness or searching for a first three-variable counterexample.
lessons.use: Start with GVC3HC: P has degree twelve and Lambda=Delta^6; the all-order written and Lean proofs are available. GVC2ENV supplies the binary closure. Retain tagged-lift failures as architecture regressions and route lower-degree work through OP-GVC3-MIN.
lessons.avoid: Repeating the 200 GF(101) cubic-profile fibres, the canonical rank-five ancilla or the literal Long tag to settle the already closed existence/dimension question.
lessons.boundary: The sixth power of a quadratic operator is not the ordinary Laplacian. Minimum degree and unclassified lift architectures remain open; a completed existence theorem does not promote the old finite-field searches.
lessons.reopen_when: A precisely stated minimum-degree or architecture-classification question requires a channel family not already excluded.

lessons.title: Preserve factorial contractions when compressing exponent lattices
lessons.when: Monomial compression or weighted channel matching is proposed as an all-order GVC transfer.
lessons.use: Prove both operator-versus-polynomial degree inequalities before replacing a contraction by matched channel counts. The cubic tagged lift forces equality and yields the explicit binomial/factorial channel sum. The weighted quartic plane instead admits unequal selections of equal weight; use its full moment equations. Keep the odd-only prime decomposition as a regression face when restoring even endpoints.
lessons.avoid: Inferring a power-compatible differential identity from an exponent-lattice parallelogram, or applying odd-face equations to the full restored coefficient space. All 56 four-term orientations are already excluded over Q by moments three or four.
lessons.boundary: A lattice compression can preserve monomials while changing their factorial weights. Field-valued disappearance of a channel does not remove its nilpotent structure from the finite moment scheme.
lessons.reopen_when: A new transfer proves the complete contraction identity and accounts for every restored channel and boundary.

lessons.title: Choose elimination pivots by downstream expansion cost
lessons.when: A multi-channel moment system has several linear pivots or a fixed rational direction slice.
lessons.use: Reuse the recorded term counts before compiling another system. For the nested degree-ten boundary, the a3 pivot gives 648/7340/15300 terms versus 958/6173/34782 for a2, so the slightly larger middle equation buys a much smaller next one. On a fixed rational cross-ratio slice compile with the numeric Gram matrix before expansion.
lessons.avoid: Selecting a pivot from one equation only, expanding the symbolic cross-ratio system before specializing a declared fibre, or treating --compile-only as a cheap metadata operation.
lessons.boundary: A rational slice is not the generic chart. Record every inverted pivot coefficient and retain its excluded projective face.
lessons.reopen_when: New moments or a different normalization change the downstream size profile, or a genuinely new chart is required.

lessons.title: Factor and rechart localization before retrying a large saturation
lessons.when: A product saturation times out on the coherent degree-ten boundary.
lessons.use: Reuse the cutoff-three factor-by-factor result: only a1 divides the original principal generator; after setting a1=1 every localization factor is coprime. At cutoff four use the recorded residual-intersection minors and solved linear D restriction to identify where growth and thickness occur.
lessons.avoid: Repeating the old 60-second product timeout with a larger limit, calling a timeout a survivor, or treating closure of all ten factor supports as construction of the saturated scheme.
lessons.boundary: Seven factors are scheme-complete in the three-prime cutoff-four calculation. The D/collision branch has normal thickness, so radical support alone loses information. These modular facts require their stated chart and primes.
lessons.reopen_when: A new residual ideal or structural representation addresses the actual unresolved localization, with a declared mathematical gate.

lessons.title: Use the next moment to close a thick fibre before building its ambient colon
lessons.when: A moment ideal has a thick normal component and further equations are available.
lessons.use: On the degree-ten nested chart, solve D=C*a0+R with C invertible and use cleared restrictions. Cutoff-four normal lengths 12 and 18 are already classified. At moment five the second restriction is a unit times e^20 and the third is a unit modulo e, where e=lam-mu. A finite geometric-series inverse closes the entire D=0 fibre, including the exceptional branch.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding a large ambient cutoff-four colon to reclose the D fibre, or replacing the finite inverse proof with a common-polynomial-gcd claim. The retained 600/900-second runs are diagnostics.
lessons.boundary: The closure holds on the declared localization. Residual D!=0, main A*B!=0 and omitted pivot/projective faces remain unresolved. Filenames ending modular3 can contain cutoff-four data; read max_order and field labels.
lessons.reopen_when: A new target concerns an unresolved residual chart or requires the ambient cutoff-four scheme itself.

lessons.title: Compute all source-degree cutoffs with one incremental echelon
lessons.when: The same tangent space is tested at many degree cutoffs for its unique source trivializer.
lessons.use: Construct the tangent basis and coefficient rows of adj(DF)G once, group the rows by source degree, then insert them in descending degree order. Rank above each cutoff gives the whole filtered profile without solving a new tangent system. Reuse the retained p=32003 profiles and CSK1 exact rational seed degrees.
lessons.avoid: Reconstructing the tangent matrix for each cutoff or redoing the rational seed gauges as if they were only modular observations.
lessons.boundary: The full cutoffs 33/48/63 remain single-prime results. Source-only first-order degree is not the optimal two-sided filtration, and finite exhaustion does not erase stable moduli or prove algebraization.
lessons.reopen_when: A characteristic-zero full-profile certificate, a new coefficient box or a precisely defined two-sided filtration is in scope.

lessons.title: Keep lower-order kernel choices in higher deformation obstructions
lessons.when: A greedy formal lift fails, or quadratic and cubic homogeneous layers are passed to a component calculation.
lessons.use: Retain the lower-order free kernel parameters when formulating the next obstruction. Use the known seed family as a positive control. The quartic generic compiler already records 22 normal quadrics and 305 cubic equations; its 327-generator homogeneous-layer input is retained, together with the failed primary-decomposition attempt.
lessons.avoid: Calling a fourth-order failure of one chosen correction a universal obstruction, identifying the layer ideal with the completed local ideal, or interpreting transverse tangent excess as proof of embedded nilpotents.
lessons.boundary: A reduced family need not be a component; excess tangent dimension can come from thickness, other branches or both. The 12 GB failed standard-basis run produced no radical or primary decomposition.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact calculation retains all lower-order choices and proves the claimed completed-scheme or algebraization implication.

lessons.title: Read terminal stopping reasons before treating unused adaptive capacity as work
lessons.when: A historical runbook calls a campaign active or quotes its maximum possible box count.
lessons.use: Use the existing terminal reporter on retained checkpoints. The record-scale cohort completed all48 curves at2352 certified boxes with zero gains; every initial no-gain wave stopped its curve. The32/8/8 score strata are fully reported. Bind roster, wave proofs, stopping reasons and completed exposure before interpreting a comparison.
lessons.avoid: Restarting a completed cohort to fill its11760-box adaptive maximum, treating a RUNNING snapshot as live state, or rebuilding the million-parameter intake to learn a retained outcome.
lessons.boundary: A completed no-gain detector result is a bounded miss. It establishes neither an upper rank bound nor score equivalence. Reporter hash checks reuse prior certificates; they are not a fresh independent arithmetic replay.
lessons.reopen_when: A different detector or population has a separately declared hypothesis, finite budget and proof plan.

lessons.title: Preserve frozen assignments while separating changed coordinate measurements
lessons.when: A historical protocol source hash differs after an explicit backend amendment.
lessons.use: Audit population, assignment, context and budgets unchanged; permit only declared source replacements whose historical bytes match the pinned revision. Keep raw and amended-runtime checkpoints separate. The rescue audit verifies the2239 assignments and historical66 clean zeros without Sage, while reporting current readiness as NOT_CERTIFIED. Preserve the exact301-class rescue set and its separate specialized reranking. The CRT half-lattice worker likewise writes a separate pointed-runtime ledger; its frozen v3 analyzer still requires the original v3 ledger.
lessons.avoid: Overwriting a frozen protocol to make its old builder --check pass, merging raw boxes into changed coordinate boxes, treating12 assigned historical zeros as12 compatible current inputs, or reconstructing absent base chunks during cleanup.
lessons.boundary: No rescue chart has run. The current worker recomputes the complete generic parity census rather than loading a persisted table. Assignment without outcome inputs does not erase that the protocol was frozen after the base checkpoint was known.
lessons.reopen_when: Compatible base evidence has been recovered and identity-checked, or a separately scoped implementation reuses a certified order keyed by exact generic Gram, basis and labels.

lessons.title: Normalize each local divisor before discarding a prime
lessons.when: An RR fake-Kummer panel rejects a place because one evaluation is nonunit or its basepoint has negative valuation.
lessons.use: Normalize the sextic and each divisor separately by rational prime powers. Omit only nonunit divisors; for negative basepoint valuation use the scalar-equivalent anchor1-T/T0. This recovered152 previously skipped pairs without new primes or points. At certified good reduction, compare the attained rank with the complete local dimension and independently check the fake kernel.
lessons.avoid: Requiring every inherited generator to be a unit, discarding a whole prime unnecessarily, or calling failure of this model reduction test intrinsic bad reduction.
lessons.boundary: The frozen panel closes553/640 pairs. The83 failed reduction tests and four anchor cases remain unresolved. Rational-scalar normalization is justified in the stated fake squareclass quotient; its true-image conclusion also uses the proved kernel statement.
lessons.reopen_when: An unresolved anchor or reduction case has a certified alternative local model, with the same class maps and completeness checks.

lessons.title: Reuse complete local images without collapsing the remaining global problem
lessons.when: A proposed RR incidence detector asks for classes outside the inherited image at an already certified place.
lessons.use: Reuse the553 complete good-prime images and all ten real and2-adic images: the inherited subgroup spans each. Preserve true/fake kernel data. A global comparison still needs simultaneous compatibility in a complete supported squareclass space, including unramified class contributions; the inherited combination can differ from place to place.
lessons.avoid: Searching for an outside-inherited class at a place already proved fully spanned, identifying local proxies with the original global fields, or replacing global completeness with trial-prime support or known rational classes.
lessons.boundary: The known rational Kummer dimension is18. A certified full Selmer dimension18 would give exact Jacobian rank18 and zero Sha[2]; a larger dimension is not automatically Sha. Prepared equation replay does not prove any local image or global Selmer group.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete global algorithm or a new unresolved-place certificate supplies an obligation beyond the already closed local panels.

lessons.title: Test proposal recall and actual integral subgroup identity before tuning scores
lessons.when: A low-height or common-cover lattice candidate is proposed as a recovered generic family.
lessons.use: Check the full proposal ledger against the frozen masked control. The two generators peak at rank12 intersections8 and10; the second comparison covers all1928 rank12 proposals, so rescoring cannot recover an absent space. Keep the successful older graph-consensus primitive closure and its index2048 actual subgroup separate. Use Curve302's completed alternative MW17 parent for construction recovery.
lessons.avoid: Promoting a containing higher-rank space to exact recovery, recognizing Fermigier from index2^11 alone, or rerunning failed proposal generators to rediscover Curve302's already proved parent.
lessons.boundary: Any independent rank-r set in one nonzero parity class forces index divisible by2^(r-1) in its primitive closure. A projected Schur quotient is not an exact integral orthogonal complement. Neither rounded heights nor bounded proposal failure proves nonexistence.
lessons.reopen_when: A new generator passes a declared control at the exact requested rank and actual integral subgroup, with a separate geometric reconstruction proof.

lessons.title: Batch coset norms and sieve exact membership while preserving relation content
lessons.when: A fixed lattice proposal searches many shifted representatives or tests a large pool against candidate spaces.
lessons.use: Precompute shifts and their norms, then evaluate each coset with q(c+s)=q(s)+2s^T Hc+q(c) and stable ordering. Reuse an exact integer kernel: mod1009 matrix products reject nonmembers before exact integer products on survivors. Keep unit relations v_i plus or minus v_j equals v_k literal; dividing content would turn a+b=2c into a false unit edge.
lessons.avoid: Repeating full norm/rank calculations for every representative, treating the support-at-most-two shifted box as complete CVP, or using bounded qfminim's second field as the minimum.
lessons.boundary: The search explicitly minimizes returned norms. Agreement of80- and100-digit height balls is numerical evidence, not an interval-certified cutoff. verify_low_height_mw_sublattices --check rebuilds balls, minima and finite reductions; it is not a cheap metadata check.
lessons.reopen_when: The exact basis or proposal domain changes, or a new completeness claim requires certified numerical bounds and an appropriately scoped replay.

lessons.title: Keep section labels and ordinate branches fixed before stacking fibres
lessons.when: Finite reductions from several parameter values are stacked to prove generic independence.
lessons.use: Use one source-root permutation and exact rational-function ordinate branches. The Mestre adapter preserves both. The corrected13 probes have rank11; the old sorted-root and positive-square-root probes still have matrix rank13 but do not specialize one common coefficient relation.
lessons.avoid: Sorting section columns independently at each fibre, choosing square-root signs numerically, or treating tests that reproduce the old matrix as a valid generic proof.
lessons.boundary: A fixed coherent matrix of full column rank plus torsion exclusion proves the stated lower bound. Rank defects alone give neither dependence nor an upper bound. The rejected entry point now fails rather than emitting a false conclusion.
lessons.reopen_when: A fixed labelled section list has a new exact certificate for the stronger claimed rank.

lessons.title: Prove recursive section identities using explicit degree bounds
lessons.when: Expanded Mestre two-section residuals would create tens or hundreds of thousands of terms.
lessons.use: Keep the monic-square and triangular ordinate recursions. Bound the numerator degree after the declared denominator clearing, then check more distinct admissible exact values than that degree. The Fermigier component uses1141 values for bound1140; the diameter235 component uses1099 for bound1080. Retain excluded poles and the leading-square condition.
lessons.avoid: Treating a Hensel or Pade fit alone as a global identity, expanding residuals unnecessarily, or dropping D=w^2 after projecting to abscissa equations.
lessons.boundary: An identity proves an incidence component, not independence of its sections. Jacobian rank and finite jets do not settle the full component without the later exact argument.
lessons.reopen_when: A changed parameterization comes with a new denominator and degree proof.

lessons.title: Separate parameter aliases and nonminimal factors from source discrepancies
lessons.when: A Fermigier specialization or raw quartic discriminant appears to give a different family or bad-fibre pattern.
lessons.use: Reuse the exact adapter u=s/2 and retained coefficients. For Y^2=X^3-27IX-27J the raw discriminant scale is(607392u)^12, since c4_raw=1296I. The twelfth-power scalar and u factor are coordinate artifacts. The exact generic arithmetic rank12 is already proved separately.
lessons.avoid: Reusing the stale202464 scale, counting literal s and adapter u as unrelated candidates, or treating completed rank computations as a resolution of the paper convention.
lessons.boundary: Literal printed shift19754/39 and reconstruction shift39508/39 give different j-invariants; the source factor-two discrepancy remains unresolved. Benchmark GP conductor calls are not metadata checks.
lessons.reopen_when: Primary-source provenance explains the convention, or an explicit new coordinate map is proved.

lessons.title: Check the target coset before lifting a missing section
lessons.when: An explicit section shell has the right rank but may have nontrivial index in its saturation.
lessons.use: Compute the exact shell lattice and target coset in the equation marking. The A11 identity shell has index five; enumerate the marked target coset to obtain the P.O=5 bridge and reuse the short group word.
lessons.avoid: Lifting an arbitrary missing-rank section or the earlier P.O=4 vector: neither necessarily generates the desired target with the retained shell.
lessons.boundary: The pole bound and coset exclusion concern this marked lattice. The orbit12 equation was subsequently constructed; the old elimination timeout is not a remaining gate.
lessons.reopen_when: A different marked subgroup or target changes the exact coset problem.

lessons.title: Reconstruct shared coefficient scales projectively
lessons.when: Exact modular section coefficients have monic denominators but coefficientwise rational reconstruction stalls.
lessons.use: Use simultaneous projective LLL on numerator and denominator coefficients, reject scales sharing a factor with the CRT modulus, then verify the rational section identity and reduction to every input prime. The q8 horizontal was recovered this way from22 primes without lifting its larger Abel trace.
lessons.avoid: Increasing all p-adic precision solely because a hidden common scale defeats independent coefficient reconstruction.
lessons.boundary: LLL proposes candidates; exact substitution and all-prime consistency certify the section. This is not a general uniqueness theorem or the subsequent RR/child construction.
lessons.reopen_when: New exact residues or a new projective normalization change the reconstruction problem.

lessons.title: Compile the chord pencil with a modular inverse
lessons.when: An exact horizontal is written x=X/Z^2, y=Y/Z^3 and the divisor ambient is known.
lessons.use: Impose AA*X=BB*Y modulo Z^2. When X is invertible modulo Z^2, solve AA=BB*Y/X modulo Z^2 directly and then impose the remaining degree and resolved vertical conditions. Verify the resulting h0=2 basis and quartic identity.
lessons.avoid: Starting a large elimination or Groebner calculation before exploiting the smooth collision congruence.
lessons.boundary: Invertibility, the complete line-bundle ambient and every vertical condition must be checked. The q8 example needs two independent resolved rows; the rootless q12 example has no vertical residual.
lessons.reopen_when: The marked divisor or its denominator/vertical support changes.

lessons.title: Certify the endpoint with the necessary construction data
lessons.when: A neighbour chain already reaches a rootless elliptic K3 equation.
lessons.use: Retain enough exact parent-to-child pointing and class transport to identify the source; recover and certify a rank17 basis directly at the endpoint. Reuse the completed source-identity, Picard-bound and saturation proofs before extending intermediate classifications.
lessons.avoid: Blocking a completed construction on an optional intermediate full MW basis, every neighbour orbit, or recovery of the entire polynomial shell.
lessons.boundary: The endpoint still needs exact equation, section identities, height Gram, source identity, Picard bound, torsion and saturation. Numerical lattice fingerprints alone do not replace those proofs.
lessons.reopen_when: The next edge or final source proof genuinely requires an omitted exact marking.

lessons.title: Compare invariant local images before refining CRT conditions
lessons.when: Comparing Kummer fingerprints across rational specializations.
lessons.use: Use the known-image source kernel at odd primes instead of raw uniformizer coordinates, which can change by a nonsquare. Use a p-maximal order at the place under audit, then freeze local-only discovery and disjoint confirmation draws before point outcomes.
lessons.avoid: Assuming t modulo p^3 fixes the desired local fingerprint, or paying for a global class/unit computation to audit one local prime.
lessons.boundary: Finite draws establish empirical stability only. The known-MW17 image is not the complete local Selmer condition.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact uniform local argument or a separately frozen parameter/prime protocol changes the gate.

lessons.title: Test detector sensitivity before interpreting a zero-event campaign
lessons.when: A bounded prospective point search returns no events.
lessons.use: Preserve the frozen cohort and protocol; apply the unchanged detector to committed positive controls and record what it actually sees. Freeze a stronger successor separately and keep binary detection, jump magnitude, upper-tail behavior and censoring gates distinct.
lessons.avoid: Treating2560 bounded misses as a rank theorem when the same call misses both known+12 controls, fitting a predictor to a constant response, or treating binary jump detection as evidence of rank32 sensitivity.
lessons.boundary: The first CRT experiment proves only its bounded zero-event outcome. The sealed MW17-only Selmer experiment has a separate unexecuted calibration gate.
lessons.reopen_when: A new detector passes predeclared controls and its compatible outcomes and inference rules are frozen.

lessons.title: Remove even uniformizer powers before evaluating cover fibres
lessons.when: Computing normalized fibres or quadratic character sums for z^2=b on a curve.
lessons.use: At an even-order zero or pole divide by its square uniformizer and evaluate the leading unit. Keep literal-square controls. On the determinant1236 candidate this repairs the false empty V4 screen and the rational fibre at4G.
lessons.avoid: Assigning character0 to every zero of b, or promoting finite Prym traces and an isomorphic cubic field to the required Shimura branch-point identity.
lessons.boundary: The candidate has exact divisor and fibre data; its particular modular CM branch-orbit identification remains open.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact characteristic-zero modular map or CM-value identity supplies the missing identification.

lessons.title: Prove omitted equations before promoting a finite lift
lessons.when: An overdetermined marked Weierstrass system has a unit maximal Jacobian minor.
lessons.use: Use the exact node/discriminant identity and prescribed jet orders to show all omitted residuals follow on the unit chart; then apply the formal implicit-function theorem. Preserve the source-shard identity and required mutual section intersections.
lessons.avoid: Treating tangent dimension one or a lift to7^8 as an infinite compatible branch, treating the branch as a QQ point, or identifying a displayed subgroup with its primitive closure.
lessons.boundary: NS0031 has a formal local branch and a separate global rational-marking exclusion. Determinant500/720 rational reconstructions saturate to the wrong determinant20 lattice.
lessons.reopen_when: A different admitted full marked curve and a new exact global rational marking change the source gate.

lessons.title: Retain specialization rank and saturation defects in the residual quotient
lessons.when: Comparing a generic subgroup, a certified specialized point group and residual Selmer dimensions.
lessons.use: First certify that the specialized generic subgroup M retains rank r. Record the free quotient rank separately from A/(M+2A), whose dimension is rank(A)-r+epsilon_M, with epsilon_M=dim A[2]+r-dim delta(M). Use a certified subgroup for lower bounds and a complete Selmer ambient space for upper bounds.
lessons.avoid: Calling an uncertified quotient gain a generic rank jump, or equating mod2 dimensions with new free directions before accounting for specialized saturation and torsion.
lessons.boundary: Generic saturation does not imply specialized saturation. Local-signature spans, incomplete descents and point-search misses do not supply a Selmer upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The generic subgroup, specialization, torsion certificate or complete Selmer ambient space changes.

lessons.title: Keep a pointed chart distinct from its actual two-covering map
lessons.when: Turning pointed quartics, translations or half-lattice search output into residual descent classes.
lessons.use: Record the birational point map phi and the actual covering map 2phi-P separately. Generic translations and the involution R->Q-R for Q in the generic subgroup preserve the residual label modulo the generic Kummer image. Deduplicate labels there, while retaining new independent point directions even when they share a label.
lessons.avoid: Treating a birational chart as the descent covering or counting every translated chart or new point as a new residual parity class.
lessons.boundary: A fixed actual two-covering maps into one coset of 2E(K). Its points can increase free rank without increasing the parity span. A coefficient-complexity claim must include the cost of the model and transport, since these can encode a known point.
lessons.reopen_when: The generic subgroup or covering cocycle changes, or a new independence certificate establishes a further free direction.

lessons.title: Use the full Cassels–Tate ambient space before claiming a rank upper bound
lessons.when: Interpreting a residual pairing matrix or selecting soluble and insoluble descent controls.
lessons.use: Certify actual Selmer membership and the Cassels–Tate construction, then distinguish the complete matrix from a restriction. A complete residual matrix of dimension s and rank 2a gives rank(E)<=r+s-2a-epsilon_M. A restricted matrix only constrains known points inside that subspace.
lessons.avoid: Using arbitrary Hilbert-symbol tensors as Cassels–Tate, treating a zero pairing or an isotropic subspace as a solubility certificate, or using a locally insoluble ambient squareclass as an insoluble Selmer control.
lessons.boundary: The residual radical modulo the full point space is 2Sha[4]; finiteness of Sha alone does not remove it. Known point classes pair to zero with all Selmer classes, so a point-only panel says nothing about the unknown complementary matrix.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual complete residual Selmer space, certified pairing entries or a new global covering witness is available.

lessons.title: Use the complete smooth-atlas obstruction before enlarging a bisection search
lessons.when: Seeking a universal rank-jump mechanism by enumerating smooth rational bisections and their generic translates on the determinant1092 parent.
lessons.use: Reuse the completed 40917-orbit quotient and its finite union of degree-two parameter images. Generic translations preserve those images. The written thin-set argument already proves that non-thin rank-at-least18 fibres remain outside the entire smooth rational atlas.
lessons.avoid: Repeating or enlarging that completed smooth rational enumeration in order to explain every rank jump, or mistaking arbitrarily many translations for new parameter coverage.
lessons.boundary: The obstruction does not locate Curve302 in the atlas, give an effective height bound or exclude singular rational curves and positive-genus covers. It also does not restrict all pointed-quartic searches to smooth rational bisections.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed construction leaves the certified smooth rational bisection class or asks a new explicitly scoped incidence question.

lessons.title: Preserve the exact fields needed for a small independent replay
lessons.when: A finite arithmetic witness reads large historical catalogues or optional local caches.
lessons.use: Extract the actual fields read by the checker, retaining unique row selectors and hashes of the original inputs and primary certificate. Provide a read-only verifier with a separate optional provenance audit. NS0031 uses eleven fields in 2771 bytes plus its 5575-byte certificate for the Clifford, 304-coset and prime19 computations.
lessons.avoid: Regenerating a missing catalogue to replay a small witness, accepting a projection with an ambiguous selector, or importing the original producer as the supposed independent implementation.
lessons.boundary: The projection preserves the selected data, not an independent proof of the source catalogue. The finite NS0031 replay does not prove the arithmetic K3 period map, global X0(37) rational-point classification, minimality or the rational37-isogenies. Optimized Python must fail before assertions can be skipped.
lessons.reopen_when: The claim, required fields or source identities change, or the separate arithmetic period-map input receives a precise proof.

lessons.title: Audit rank-screen identities and censoring before replaying calculations
lessons.when: Reusing a bounded rank screen or interpreting a command named --check.
lessons.use: Read the checker body and validate the complete roster, per-case input and execution identities, interval types, summary and ranking from the stored rows. Keep completed intervals, singleton exact ranks and censored cases as different counts. The V4 screen has62 completed intervals,17 exact ranks and2 named timeouts.
lessons.avoid: Trusting a saved total after checking only input hashes, counting timeout as rank zero, or rerunning the entire screen to inspect two unresolved cases.
lessons.boundary: A record audit does not independently prove PARI rank bounds. The original10-second limit includes Sage startup. Base-Jacobian rank and product-twist rank are separate questions; the later rank-zero product target55 does not settle timeout cases3 or30.
lessons.reopen_when: A new scoped calculation supplies a rank certificate for a specific unresolved curve or the stored universe/input identities change.

lessons.title: Reuse regulator squareclass obstructions before a full descent
lessons.when: A product twist has certified good reductions of analytic rank one and a height-preserving specialization argument.
lessons.use: A hypothetical nontorsion section forces rank equality at each usable prime. Refined BSD then gives its height the squareclass of p^(chi-1)*L_star/product(c_v). Incompatible squareclasses exclude every rational height. Reuse the completed17-product closure and empty section queue.
lessons.avoid: Launching the old height-eight/height-ten solver or complete Selmer calculation after arithmetic rank zero is proved, or using an analytic-rank-two row in a rank-one height comparison.
lessons.boundary: Count each closed-place Tamagawa factor once. The argument needs complete certified L-polynomials, good reduction, height preservation and the stated finite-function-field theorem. Arithmetic rank zero does not imply geometric rank zero or Sha[2]=0.
lessons.reopen_when: A different target survives the exact eligible-prime comparison or the specialization hypotheses differ.

lessons.title: Use the full integral involution module for the Tate quotient
lessons.when: Computing a product-character obstruction from invariant and anti-invariant sections.
lessons.use: For a saturated basis B of ker_Z(1+S), solve 1-S=B*D integrally and compute coker(D); Smith factors are1 or2. The quotient can be represented by F2 functionals on the anti-invariant coordinates. If a stronger theorem already gives A-=0, conclude the quotient is zero directly.
lessons.avoid: Substituting a visible eigensublattice for the full MW group, equating a Selmer candidate space with the point-Kummer image, or taking exclusion of the zero class as existence of a nonzero class.
lessons.boundary: The supplied lattice must be full; checking S^2=1 and its Gram isometry cannot prove arithmetic fullness. All17 old products are arithmetically closed, although full Selmer groups were not computed.
lessons.reopen_when: A new target has a certified full involution lattice or complete actual point-Kummer image.
